title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the end of a 1965 typed letter. It finishes an argument begun on the previous page about how mod-p étale cohomology relates to de Rham cohomology in characteristic p.

Setting: X is smooth over a perfect field k of characteristic p > 0. On the previous page, Grothendieck builds a map H^*(X, F_p) -> H^*_dR(X).
- De Rham cohomology can be computed in the étale topology. Each term of the complex is quasi-coherent, so étale and Zariski cohomology agree.
- The map then comes from the 'conjugate' spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p(X, H^q(Omega^.)) => H^{p+q}_dR(X).
- It factors as H^*(X, F_p) -> H^*(X, O_X) -> H^*_dR(X). The second arrow is the edge map of the conjugate spectral sequence. It uses the Cartier-type isomorphism O_X -> H^0(Omega^.), f |-> f^p: O_{X'} identifies with the sheaf of closed functions O_X^p.

There is also an edge map H^n_dR(X) -> H^n(X, O_X) from the other (Hodge-to-de Rham) spectral sequence.

This page claims that the composite H^n(X, O_X) -> H^n_dR(X) -> H^n(X, O_X) 'can hardly be anything other than' Frobenius.
- In modern terms: at the level of complexes, O_X -> Omega^. sends f to f^p (landing in degree 0, in closed forms). Projection Omega^. -> O_X is the identity in degree 0. So the composite of sheaf maps is f |-> f^p, the absolute Frobenius. It therefore induces the p-linear Frobenius F on H^n(X, O_X).
- Combined with Artin–Schreier, the image of H^n(X, F_p) lands in the Frobenius-fixed part. This is Serre's 1958 picture (Mexico paper).

Grothendieck then dismisses all this as 'bien éculé' (well-worn). He says genuinely new things will come only from the 'true' p-adic cohomology, i.e. the crystalline theory he was developing in 1965–66. The letter closes with 'Bien cordialement'.
errors: No mathematical error. The hedge 'ne peut guère être autre chose' is overly cautious: the composite is exactly the absolute Frobenius, by a one-line check on complexes, since f |-> f^p followed by projection to degree 0 is f |-> f^p.

Minor imprecision: H^0(Omega^.) is isomorphic to O_{X'} (Frobenius twist) as a module. The identification with O_X via f |-> f^p is only p-linear, hence 'Frobenius-semilinear' maps. This is implicit in the text.

ideas.what: The composite H^n(O_X) -> H^n_dR -> H^n(O_X), built from the edge maps of the conjugate and Hodge spectral sequences, equals Frobenius.
ideas.modern_name: Edge maps of the conjugate and Hodge-de Rham spectral sequences; absolute Frobenius on H^n(O_X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier (1957) for the Cartier isomorphism; Katz (1970, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem') for the conjugate spectral sequence and its relation to the Hodge filtration; Serre (1958) for Frobenius on H^n(O)
ideas.where_published: Not as such. Related material is in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) and Berthelot–Ogus.

ideas.what: The map H^*(X, F_p) -> H^*(X, O_X) -> H^*_dR(X), via étale computation of de Rham cohomology.
ideas.modern_name: Artin–Schreier sequence, plus the comparison of mod-p étale cohomology with the Frobenius-fixed part of coherent/de Rham cohomology
ideas.where_published: SGA 4½ / SGA 7 contain related Artin–Schreier statements (unsure about this exact formulation)

ideas.what: The call for a 'true' p-adic cohomology as the only route to new results.
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the closing page of a letter. Its content is a routine, well-known observation, which Grothendieck himself calls 'éculé': the Cartier/conjugate edge map composed with the Hodge edge map is Frobenius. The final remark points to crystalline cohomology, which he soon developed and published.
transcription_corrections: 'qu'on ne pourra dire [-deux-] des choses' -> in the typescript a word (apparently 'deux') is struck out by typed-over 'x' characters. Read: 'qu'on ne pourra dire des choses vraiment intéressantes'.
'p-adique' is typed with an overstruck character in place of the hyphen ('p·adique'); the reading 'p-adique' is correct.
'Bien cordialement' is followed by a period/comma mark; no signature appears on this page.
